name: Saints Joachim and Anne
dates: First century BC · Parents of the Blessed Virgin
history: The parents of the Virgin Mary and grandparents of Jesus. Their names are not in Scripture but come from an ancient tradition recorded in the second century. They are honoured as a holy couple who waited long for a child and offered her to God. They are patrons of grandparents, and the Church keeps a World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly near their feast.
life: The second-century writing known as the Protoevangelium of James tells that Joachim, a wealthy and devout man, and his wife Anne were childless into old age, and that Joachim was turned away from offering his gift in the Temple because of it. He went into the wilderness to fast and pray, and Anne prayed at home, and an angel told each of them that they would have a child. They met at the Golden Gate of Jerusalem in joy, and Mary was born to them. The story is not Scripture, and the Church does not vouch for its details, but it carries a true instinct: that Mary was prepared for by a faithful family. Devotion to Anne grew in the East from the sixth century and spread through the West in the Middle Ages, being especially strong in medieval England. Great shrines to her stand at Auray in Brittany and Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré in Canada.
prayerTo: Saint Joachim and Saint Anne, you waited in faith and raised the Mother of God in a home of prayer. Pray for grandparents and the elderly, for couples who long for children, and for every family. Help me to hand on the faith to those who come after me. Amen.
penance: Visit, call or write to a grandparent or an elderly person today. If your grandparents have died, pray for them by name.
meditation: The grace given to Mary passed through an ordinary home. What are you handing on to the next generation?
prayer: O God, Who in Your kindness gave blessed Anne the grace to be the mother of her who mothered Your only-begotten Son, graciously grant that we who keep her feast may be helped by her intercession with You. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
